summary: Cape St. Marys light on St. Mary's Bay, Nova Scotia, was first lit in 1868; the Robichau family kept it for 62 years, and the Municipality of Clare took it over in 2017.

light.fog_signal: diaphone (added 1915 per Lighthouse Friends; society gives 1914)

structures.note: Lighthouse Friends gives 13.1 m (43 ft); the society's entry gives 46 ft (about 14 m). Story uses 13.1 m.
The register calls the present tower the third on the site. The society dates a second tower to between 1883 and 1922 and gives no firmer date.
Built into the corner of a concrete-block fog-alarm building; red octagonal lantern. Society dates it 1965; register says the features follow Department of Transport drawings of 1968.

access.note: Municipal park with parking, interpretive panels, benches and picnic tables. Grounds open, tower closed (Lighthouse Friends).

facts.agency: Municipality of the District of Clare (owner since 2017); light listed by the Canadian Coast Guard

events.note: Board of Works of Nova Scotia awards a $2,800 contract, 26 June 1867, to Dexter and Robichau; the light is finished after Nova Scotia joins Canada
First light shown; wooden octagonal tower 13.1 m high
Wooden octagonal tower with keeper's dwelling 10 m by 6.7 m (33 by 22 ft) built near it

Diaphone fog signal in a gabled building, 1915 per Lighthouse Friends; society gives 1914; Department list for year ended 31 March 1915 marks the station F. A.; the list for year ended 31 March 1914 has no mark
Present square concrete tower built into a one-storey building (1969 per Lighthouse Friends; 1965 per society)
De-staffed 31 March 1989; the last keepers left
Keeper's dwelling moved to Middle West Pubnico
Keeper's dwelling set off in October 2009 for a new site on Canoe Island, off Abbott's Harbour
Municipality of Clare takes possession of the light and 2.1 acres on 10 January 2017, under a federal divestiture process
Park work begins the following summer: parking, interpretive panels, benches, picnic tables; tower shingled and painted

keepers.name: Mathurin Robichau
keepers.note: First keeper. Former sea captain, elected for Clare to the Nova Scotia assembly in 1855, who left politics a year after Confederation to take the light (Lighthouse Friends). Salary $500. Also spelled Robicheau and Robichaud in the Department's tables.

keepers.name: Benjamin H. Robichau
keepers.note: Son of Mathurin; one of seven children. Lighthouse Friends gives 1886 to 1931. The Department's keeper table for the year ended 30 June 1906 has 'Robicheau, B. H.' at Cape St. Mary, and the table for the year ended 31 March 1910 has 'Benj. H. Robichaud'.

keepers.name: B. A. Melanson
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends lists him for 1931 only.

keepers.name: Marco Frontain
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends prints a 1950 photograph of him in the lighthouse garden.

keepers.name: Bill R. Goodwin
keepers.note: Lighthouse Friends lists him 1983 to 1987 and again 1987 to 1988, with Mary Louise Goodwin listed in 1987 between the two.

keepers.name: Mary Louise Goodwin
keepers.note: One of twelve keepers between 1868 and 1988, and the only woman among them according to Lighthouse Friends, which calls her Mary Goodwin in the text.

corrections.proposed: Municipality of the District of Clare
corrections.why: The record's agency is cut off mid-name. The society and Lighthouse Friends give the owner as the Municipality of the District of Clare, which took possession on 10 January 2017.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The record lists different first years. The register, Lighthouse Friends and the society all give 1868 as the first light on the site. The 1969 tower is the present one, and the society dates a second tower between 1883 and 1922.

notes_for_editor: (1) Keeper names in the Department's tables (1906, 1910, 1915) were matched by position in OCR, since the station and keeper columns are printed as separate blocks. The 1906 entry 'Robicheau, B. H' and the 1910 entry 'Benj. H. Robichaud' should be checked on scan pages 183 and 256 before the spelling is treated as settled. (2) The fog-signal date conflicts: Lighthouse Friends 1915, the society 1914. The Department's list for the year ended 31 March 1914 has no fog mark for the station, and the list for 31 March 1915 has one. The story gives the Department's wording. (3) The present tower: 1969 (Lighthouse Friends, and the register's 1968 drawings) against 1965 (society). The story uses 1969. (4) The first tower's height: 13.1 m (Lighthouse Friends) against 46 ft (society), about 14 m. (5) The second tower is undated beyond the society's 1883 to 1922 span. Reports for the 1880s and 1890s are not in the local corpus. (6) Lighthouse Friends says the light is owned by the Canadian Coast Guard, which conflicts with its own account of the 2017 transfer to the municipality. The story follows the 2017 transfer, which the society also gives. (7) The record's 2016 heritage designation date does not appear in the register text I read, so it is not in the story. (8) No dated storm, wreck or rescue at the station was found in the sources consulted, so the Storms chapter is left out. (9) 'Cape Cove (Cape St. Mary)' appears in the Department's 1915 keeper list under B. Doucette (1907). It may be a separate light and is not used. (10) Keepers after 1959 are named only as Lighthouse Friends names them, in the role it gives, with no personal detail. (11) No photos sourced.
